$comment: Conversation quality rubric examples for test/eval-rubric.test.js (Agent Brain v2.1, T16).
title: ATLAS conversation rubric: annotated examples and deterministic linter expectations
disclaimer: REGRESSION AID, NOT A HUMAN RATING. The 1 to 5 'rating' of each example is one engineer's annotation against 07_Evaluation_and_QA/ATLAS_Evaluation_Framework.md section 2, made when the file was written. The linter in test/eval-rubric.test.js is a set of deterministic string rules (question count, banned praise, leading closed question, praise before basis, repeated known fact, therapy tone, and two extras: empty praise, form commands, identity praise). It cannot judge warmth, curiosity or whether a reply fits the conversation. It exists so that a change to ATLAS's wording or guard that reintroduces a known anti-pattern fails a test. Conversation quality with real consultants must be rated by people, with pilot users, before any broad rollout (release gate 7). This rubric evaluates the agent, never a consultant.

scale.1: robotic checklist, leading questions, repeats known facts
scale.3: polite and mostly relevant, some generic questions
scale.5: warm, context-aware, one high-value open question at a time; natural reactions used sparingly; probes only where needed

sources.good: quoted from the v2.1 pack (Conversation Examples, Personality doc, MAAP spec)
sources.bad: the pack's own 'Bad' lines (Personality doc section 9) plus lines authored from the rubric's level-1 description, marked 'authored'

items.speaker: atlas
items.text: Hi! I'm Atlas. I'm here to help capture the work you've done and make sure the experience is represented properly. We'll have a conversation about the project, your contribution and what changed because of it. I'll ask follow-up questions where something deserves a little more detail, and if something is client-confidential, just say so and I'll note it without the details. At the end, I'll summarise what I heard so you can correct it before it goes for review. To start, could you tell me about the project you're working on?
items.note: Seven sentences: too long for one spoken turn (the shipped opening is two pieces); the content is the pack's, with its "skip anything you don't know or can't share" clause replaced by the confidentiality line (Tony, 2026-10-31, DECISION_LOG D-U2-1).
